# Vendoring notes for Excalidraw

Generated by `scripts/vendor-excalidraw.mjs` (`npm run vendor:excalidraw`). Do not hand-edit
the `.js`/`.css` files in this directory — regenerate them instead. After regeneration, run
`npm run patch:excalidraw-tools` to apply the reproducible compatibility patch described below.

**Pinned at**: `@excalidraw/excalidraw@0.18.1`, `react@19.2.8`, `react-dom@19.2.8` (see
`package.json` devDependencies for the versions actually used to produce the committed output —
bump those, `npm install`, then re-run the vendor script).

## Why this isn't a plain file download

Excalidraw's npm package ships ESM output (`dist/prod/index.js`) that imports ~20 transitive
packages as bare specifiers (`clsx`, `jotai`, `roughjs`, `@radix-ui/react-popover`, etc.), not
just `react`/`react-dom`. Their own docs' "embed without a bundler" path relies on an ESM CDN
(`esm.sh`) transitively resolving all of those; vendoring the raw file locally would leave every
one of them unresolved in a browser. `scripts/vendor-excalidraw.mjs` runs esbuild once (a
one-time generation step, not a runtime build — same role `build_db.js` plays for
`js/code_db.js`) to inline all of that into a single `excalidraw.js`, keeping only
`react`/`react-dom`/`react-dom/client`/`react/jsx-runtime` external.

## Three real bugs hit while building this, worth knowing before touching the script

1. **`export * from 'react'` silently drops every named export except `default`.** esbuild's
   CJS-named-export detection didn't reliably see through a wildcard re-export for the `react`
   package specifically. Fix: enumerate every name explicitly in both the `import {...}` and
   `export {...}` clauses (see `REACT_NAMES` in the vendor script).

2. **`Dynamic require of "react" is not supported` at runtime, despite `window.require` being
   set.** Root cause: react-dom's *own* bundled internals contain `require("react")` calls
   nested inside a lazily-invoked CommonJS module factory — not written by us, invisible to any
   import declaration our own entry file writes. esbuild only hoists a `require()` call to a
   static ESM `import` when it's a syntactically-obvious top-level reference; it does not do so
   for calls buried in a dependency's own wrapped-CJS body. The result: **zero** static `import
   ... from "react"` statement anywhere in `react-dom.js`'s output, so nothing in the ES module
   spec's "dependencies evaluate before dependents" guarantee applied — `react.js`'s
   `window.require` shim (see bug 3) had no guaranteed ordering relative to when react-dom's
   internals first called it.

   Fix: force a **real, used** static import of `react` in the react-dom entry file
   (`import __reactForLoadOrder from 'react'; export const __reactLoadOrderGuard = ...`) — an
   *unused* bare `import 'react';` gets tree-shaken away by esbuild for external packages, so it
   has to actually be exported to survive.

3. **Bare `process` references throw in a browser.** React/react-dom's CJS source does
   `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') { ... } else { ... }` unconditionally (no
   `typeof process !== 'undefined'` guard in some spots). esbuild does not auto-define
   `process.env.NODE_ENV`; must pass `--define:process.env.NODE_ENV='"production"'` explicitly
   so the minifier dead-code-eliminates the branch instead of leaving a runtime reference to a
   Node global that doesn't exist in a browser.

## What's vendored vs. not

- `react.js`, `react-dom.js` (serves both the `react-dom` and `react-dom/client` specifiers —
  see the script's comment on why they're bundled together), `react-jsx-runtime.js`,
  `excalidraw.js`: all self-contained, minified, ESM.
- `excalidraw.css` + `fonts/`: copied verbatim from `dist/prod` (~17MB, mostly font files for
  Excalidraw's several hand-drawn/code font families) — **not yet trimmed**; a reasonable
  follow-up is checking which font families the app actually renders with by default and
  dropping the rest, but correctness came first.
- `dist/prod/locales/` (Excalidraw's own UI i18n strings): **not vendored** — its own toolbar
  UI defaults to English, which is acceptable for now since this site has its own separate
  i18n system for everything outside the canvas.
- LICENSE files for all three (`LICENSE-excalidraw`, `LICENSE-react`, `LICENSE-react-dom`) — all
  MIT. Excalidraw's npm package doesn't ship a LICENSE file itself; that one was pulled directly
  from `github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/master/LICENSE`, not regenerated by the script.

## `_smoke_test.html`

A minimal standalone page (import map + `createRoot(...).render(<Excalidraw />)`, no app
integration) that mounts nothing but this vendored bundle. Open it directly whenever
re-vendoring to sanity-check the output before touching any app wiring — it's what caught all
three bugs above. Keep it; it's cheap insurance.

## Local integration patch

The vendored wrapper in this pinned build drops every `UIOptions.tools` flag except `image`
when it creates the internal prop object. `scripts/patch-excalidraw-tools.mjs` preserves those
flags so the Student Runtime can expose a layout-only Canvas for Scenarios with
`editInput: false`. Run it after every vendor regeneration; the script fails closed if the
upstream bundle shape changes.
